statement.excerpt: Instead, part of the actual outcome over the next few years will be that both countries build a lot of generative AI infrastructure — quite possibly significantly more than they actually need.
statement.document_title: The core misconception that is driving American AI policy

from_speaker: build a lot of generative AI infrastructure
quite possibly significantly more than they actually need
our_interpretation: 'Both countries' means the United States and China.
The firm part of the forecast is that both countries build a lot of generative AI infrastructure, such as data centres, GPU clusters and power capacity for AI, over the next few years.

The excess part ('quite possibly significantly more than they actually need') is hedged. It is a possibility, not a firm prediction. It is not required for support, and its failure would not count as a contradiction.
'Next few years' is read as roughly three to five years from December 2025. The latest plausible end is the end of 2030.
criteria.support_condition: By the end of the horizon, public records such as company capex filings, official statistics, or data-centre construction and commissioning trackers show that both the US and China built large amounts of generative AI infrastructure during the few years after December 2025.
criteria.contradiction_condition: By the end of the horizon, records show that either the US or China built only modest new generative AI infrastructure during the period, for example after a sharp, sustained collapse in AI data-centre buildout.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Capex filings from US and Chinese cloud and AI companies, official statistics, and data-centre capacity trackers covering roughly 2026–2028 (up to 2030).
